label: last copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires almost only on the final output step of length-3 sequences (t=5, input = 2nd original token fed back, outputting the 3rd original token); ~96% of such steps are active and they hold ~93% of activation mass, covering essentially all of the top two activation quartiles. Never active in the original or delimiter phases, nor on first-occurrence inputs. Remaining ~7% of mass is weak activations (<~0.15 of max) scattered over copy-phase steps of longer sequences, mostly at or near the final step (to_go 0-2). Magnitude only weakly varies with the input token (3, l, r, u, z inputs among the top). False positives are a few L=3 final steps with inputs like a, d, f.

issues: Provenance is unverified. The user asked for the baseline on the subsampled data in features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5, but every score here came from features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store, and I was not allowed to check whether that store was built from the 1/5 data. The interpretation holds for that store. Whether it answers the user's request is still unconfirmed.

'Never active when the input is a token's first appearance' is true but trivial. In the copy phase in_first is always 0, because every fed-back input repeats an original token, so the predicate selects 0 steps. It adds no information.

'Magnitude depends only weakly on input token (3, l, r, u, z top)' comes from the pooled profile. That profile mixes the L=3 core with the weak tail, where inputs l and 3 are over-represented among the misses. Treating l/3 at to_go 0 in longer sequences as a secondary trigger only reaches about 4% precision, though, so it is not a real secondary class.

Recall of 0.744 means about 26% of active steps (857 test steps, 6.8% of mass) fall outside the predicate. They are diffuse weak activations on the final 1-2 steps of L>=4 sequences (to_go==0 holds 98.5% of mass overall but has only 1.6% precision). Restricting to particular lengths (6/7/9), input tokens, repeated tokens (in_count>1) or copy errors (correct==0) did not isolate them. So this is a low-rate tail, not a systematic missed class.
False positives (113 test steps, about 4% of L=3/t=5) are scattered across tokens with no visible pattern.
